traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.35, 0.13, 0.08], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.height_max_m.note: Sargent (1922): usually 40 to 50 ft tall, occasionally 70 to 80 ft (converted: 12.192 to 15.24 m, occasionally 21.336 to 24.384 m). Silvics vol. 1 (1990) says it rarely exceeds 15 m, the record tree is 18 m, and trees over 12 m are rare; Abrams vol. 1 gives 10 to 25 m.

generator.params.bend_set.note: Conifer sag (M6, bend@1): the share of each year's sag its wood keeps, with `straighten` the share of that bend it straightens each year. Set by eye from renders at 60 to 80 years: with the program's creep (0.5 and 0.02) the Pacific yew's thin, slow limbs hang down, so it keeps the milder creep the broadleaf program uses (0.1 and 0.3).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Taxus brevifolia (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.58 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 3 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.58, branches 0.6. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 51): needles flat, 12 to 16 mm, kept four or five years; the seed about 8 mm, in a scarlet cup-shaped aril.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's Pacific yew review: needles 1 to 3 cm; Abrams's 12 to 16 mm is the usual range.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: FEIS's Pacific yew review: needles kept at least five or six years; Abrams gives four or five.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, slow, often crooked understory tree with long, drooping branches and flat sprays of soft, pointed needles. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): seeds in a red fleshy aril about 8 mm; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage; `branch_ageing` is gone with the calendar ageing it set.

allometry.note: Trunk: Busing and Spies (1995) measured Pacific yew in mature and old-growth stands of western Oregon and Washington growing 0 to 3 cm in diameter at breast height a decade; at the middle of that, 1.5 cm a decade, a yew is 12 cm across at 80 years. The 25 cm before was a rough size from general knowledge. Height: still a rough size from general knowledge, 9 m at 80 years, inside FEIS's 6 to 12 m at maturity (250 to 350 years); replace with measured data.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark yellowish-green needles; thin, scaly, reddish-purple bark. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): flat needles 1 to 3 cm long and about 2 mm wide, so a needle 0.09 as wide as it is long (`width`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): thin purplish scales peeling to show red inner bark; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
